result.rationale: The diff's refreshOAuthTokens, in the credential-sync branch, returns the raw `fetch` Response (`return response;` after `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, ...)`). Callers pipe this into code that expects the original SDK/axios shapes: zoho-bigin/zohocrm check `tokenInfo.data.error`, googlecalendar reads `res?.data` then `token.access_token`, hubspot reads `hubspotRefreshToken.expires_in`. When the sync endpoint is configured, these accesses operate on a Response object, so `.data` is undefined and refresh breaks — a real correctness defect introduced by this diff, per the dif

judged_text: refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response in sync mode, which doesn't match callers expecting axios/SDK shapes: zoho-bigin and zohocrm read tokenInfo.data.error (TypeError), googlecalendar reads res?.data (undefined, access_token throws), and hubspot reads expires_in (undefined, persisting expiryDate = NaN) — token refresh is broken for these apps when CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is set

adjudication.rationale: `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the raw `fetch(...)` `Response` when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts). Multiple callers in this diff still treat the return value as an axios/SDK result shape: Google Calendar uses `res?.data` and then `token.access_token` (packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts), Zoho Bigin/Zoho CRM read `tokenInfo.data.error` / `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error` (packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts, packages/app-store/zohocrm/lib/CalendarService.ts), and Hubspot assigns `HubspotToken` from the return and then uses token fields (packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts). In sync mode these will be `undefined`/TypeErrors because a `fetch` Response doesn't have `.data` or those SDK fields, so token refresh breaks when `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is set.
